findings.text: Fallback SVA configuration provides no-op or failing operations: device bind reports device absence, unbind and pasid drop and KVA range invalidate do nothing, pasid getters report the invalid marker, and mm init and valid test report absence of PASID state.

A freshly duplicated address space must clear its IOMMU mm association so parent and child do not share one instance with double release risk; validity means that association is present, and the enqueue-command PASID accessor returns invalid when absent and otherwise the stored PASID.

Fallback page-fault queue configuration cannot service devices: queue attach, device flush, allocation failure handling, partial discard and fault report signal absence or null, while queue free, device detach, group free, group response and group dequeue are silent no-ops.

Sleeping poll helper repeatedly performs an operation then tests a condition until success or expiry. It optionally sleeps before first iteration, enforces ordering so operation and condition observe expiry, relaxes the CPU each lap, sleeps between laps, reports success as zero and expiry as timed out, and treats zero timeout as never expiring.

Atomic poll helper has the same repeat operation then test contract but never sleeps: it uses busy microsecond delays, optionally delays before first iteration, tracks remaining nanoseconds by subtracting delays plus a per-lap tick, and likewise returns zero on condition and timed out on expiry with zero timeout meaning unbounded.

Read-poll convenience wrappers bind a read operation result into a variable and forward to the sleeping or atomic poll helpers; address-taking forms fix the pre-read flag to false and typed byte, word, long and quad accessors including relaxed variants supply the corresponding read operation.

Resource record holds inclusive start and end addresses, a name pointer, flag and descriptor words, and parent, sibling and child links forming a tree. Constraint record holds minimum, maximum and alignment plus an alignment callback and its opaque data; the callback maps opaque data to an aligned size type.

Primary resource flag layout reserves low bus bits, a type field, and modifier bits for prefetch, readonly, cacheable, range length, shadowable, size and start alignment, 64-bit memory, bridge window, software mux, extended system RAM variants and driver-managed or mergeable RAM, plus exclusive, disabled, unset, auto and busy states; system RAM is the combination of memory and system RAM types.

Bus-specific subfields encode interrupt trigger and polarity plus shareable, optional and wake-capable hints; DMA width, master, transfer unit and speed types; memory writability, cacheability, range length, width mask, shadowability, expansion ROM and non-posted behavior; port address width, fixed and sparse flags; ROM enable and shadow flags; and PCI fixed and equivalent-indicator flags.

Resource descriptor enumeration distinguishes none, crash kernel, ACPI tables, ACPI nonvolatile storage, persistent memory and legacy persistent memory, device private memory, reserved, soft reserved and CXL; mapping flags distinguish system RAM mapping and encrypted mapping.

Resource construction and query rules: end is start plus size minus one with IRQ and DMA using unit size; size is end minus start plus one; type and extended type are flag masks; containment requires equal types and inclusive bounds plus set addresses; overlap is interval intersection; intersection and union fill a result only on overlap; assigned means linked to a parent; disabled IRQ records equal start and end with IRQ, disabled and unset flags.

Region management macros target the global port and memory roots: plain, muxed and exclusive request forms, release forms, device-managed request and release forms, and a rename operation that replaces the stored name pointer.

I/O priority packs class and level with a none hint for the default; a value is valid only when its class is above none and at most idle; nice level derives from the CPU nice offset into bands of five; scheduling class maps idle tasks to idle, realtime or deadline tasks to realtime, and others to best effort; without block context the task priority is always the default and capability checks report unsupported block operation.

Reading another task I/O context priority requires holding that task allocation lock; the current task is exempt. Missing context or none class falls back to the nice-derived class and level, and the current-task accessor forwards to this helper.
System memory mapping handle is a discriminated union holding either an I/O memory address or a plain CPU address plus a boolean selecting the I/O memory interpretation.

IORemap address range aliases the start and end of the virtual allocation range; one configuration tests membership after stripping address tags with inclusive start and exclusive end, while the alternate configuration reports every address as outside the range.

The sleeping poll path may sleep between iterations and before the first operation, so it must not be used where sleeping is forbidden; the atomic path avoids that hazard by busy waiting but consumes CPU while polling.
